title: Diamond Sutra 11, 无为福胜: rivers of rivers, and a sentence that beats the count
desc: 有为 giving is measurable; 无为 is outside the frame. The comparison is not big gift vs small gift but giving inside the counting frame vs outside it.

title: Diamond Sutra 12, 尊重正教: the place where four lines are spoken
desc: 随说: no preferred venue, no curated audience. 供养 is respect, not exchange. 经典所在即为有佛 means where the meaning is carried — not that paper holds a buddha.

title: Diamond Sutra 13, 如法受持: the sutra names itself, then cancels the name
desc: 金刚般若波罗蜜, then 即非…是名 applied to the title itself. 奉持 is holding the meaning; 如来无所说; 微尘 and 世界 both conditional.

title: Diamond Sutra 14, 离相寂灭: 须菩提 weeps, and 忍辱 is not submission
desc: 实相即是非相. 忍辱波罗蜜 is not endurance: it is the absence of the two fixed positions, harmed and harming — defence still allowed, the stored injury gone.

title: Diamond Sutra 15, 持经功德: three times a day, for aeons, and 信心不逆
desc: Morning, noon, evening; bodies like Ganges sands, for 百千万亿劫. 信心不逆 — the mind does not push back — already outweighs it. 荷担如来: carried on the shoulder.

title: Diamond Sutra 16, 能净业障: being despised, and heavy karma made light
desc: 重业轻受, and its boundary: the claim concerns the inner ledger, not a licence to accept abuse. 不可思议 means outside accounting, not wishes granted.

title: Diamond Sutra 17, 究竟无我: the question from section 2, answered differently
desc: The same question, after fifteen sections of dismantling. 实无有法发菩提心者; 如来者即诸法如义; 无实无虚; even 无我 not held as a dharma.

title: Diamond Sutra 18, 一体同观: five eyes, and a mind that cannot be found
desc: 肉眼天眼慧眼法眼佛眼: apertures, not superpowers — 佛眼 is not being stuck in any of the four. Then 过去心不可得, 现在心不可得, 未来心不可得.

title: Diamond Sutra 19, 法界通化: if merit were real, it would not be called great
desc: 若福德有实，如来不说得福德多. Great only because it has no substance. 福德无 is not 福德空: effects remain exact, the account book closes.

title: Diamond Sutra 20, 离色离相: even a perfect body is still a body
desc: 具足色身 and 具足诸相 — the fullest form in the tradition, still 即非. If the perfected body is not the ground, no improvement of form will be.
